Solo Road Trip · October 2026

Cali's Oregon Road Trip

Six nights, one Tesla, and the inland run up I-5 from the Bay Area to Portland — Mount Shasta, Crater Lake, Ashland, Eugene, and the Columbia Gorge, all before the rain rolls in.

Day 1 · Saturday

San Francisco → Mount Shasta

Two real stops today, not just a drive — a waterfall hike and a lake, so the first day earns its miles.

6:00am depart~215 mi

Depart San Francisco

Early start beats the Sacramento Valley heat and gets you to Redding by late morning. Top off charge at home overnight — every percent matters on the non-long-range Model Y.

Redding Supercharger + lunch

Charge here — it's the last reliable fast-charging stop before Mount Shasta (~62 mi, comfortable, but top off anyway since the next gap after that is longer). Quick lunch while you wait, then keep moving.

Afternoon2–3.6 mi

McCloud Falls

Three waterfalls (Lower, Middle, Upper) connected by an easy trail along the McCloud River, about 10 minutes past Mount Shasta town. You can do all three round trip (~3.6 mi) or just Lower + Middle if you're short on daylight — either way it's a much better stretch-your-legs stop than another rest area.

Lake Siskiyou → camp

Swim or watch the sunset over the lake with Mount Shasta rising straight out of the water behind it, then set up at Lake Siskiyou Camp Resort. Charge fully before you park; Camp Mode runs all night.

Mount Shasta → Ashland, OR

Shorter drive, more time on the ground in Ashland before settling in for the night.

Downtown Mount Shasta

Berryvale Grocery has a solid espresso counter and grab-and-go breakfast — worth 30–45 minutes before getting back on the road.

Charge stop

Medford Supercharger

The Mount Shasta→Medford stretch crosses the Siskiyou Summit grade, which eats more range than flat highway miles. This Supercharger (near the OR-62 / Crater Lake Highway junction) is 15 minutes from Ashland and doubles as tomorrow's launch point toward Crater Lake.

AfternoonFree

Lithia Park

A 100-acre park running straight through downtown Ashland along Ashland Creek — duck ponds, a Japanese garden, lawns, shaded paths. Easy, flat walking that lets out right into Ashland's restaurant row.

Dinner, then camp at Emigrant Lake

Ashland punches well above its size for food — it's a Shakespeare Festival town with the restaurant scene to match. Charge at the Medford Supercharger on the way to camp.

Day 3 · Monday

Crater Lake → Roseburg (through, not back)

The old version of this day drove to Crater Lake and doubled back to the same area — a wasted half-day of driving with nothing new to show for it. This version goes through the park and comes out the other side, making real progress north.

Charge before you goNo Supercharging in-park

Top off at the Medford Supercharger

No fast charging inside Crater Lake, and today covers the park plus a full drive out the north side to Roseburg — leave with a full charge.

🚘
~1.5–2 hr · OR-62 south entrance
$30 vehicle feeRim Drive

Crater Lake National Park

Rim Drive is typically open early July through late October, weather permitting — worth checking conditions the morning of. Rim Village and Discovery Point are the easiest overlooks; Watchman Overlook has the best view of Wizard Island. In-park camping closes for the season by late September, which is why this stays a drive-through, not an overnight.

Map it →
↗
Exit north · onto Hwy 138 W (Rogue-Umpqua Scenic Byway), no backtrack
~45 min in0.4 mi round trip

Toketee Falls

A short, easy walk to a striking two-tiered 113-ft waterfall through columnar basalt — one of the most photographed falls in Oregon, and it's directly on the route out of the park. Susan Creek Falls is a similar quick stop a bit further down the same highway if you want a second one.

Map it →

~1.25 hr · Hwy 138 W into Roseburg
NightCamp

Camp near Roseburg

There's riverside camping right along the Umpqua at Amacher Park / Whistlers Bend, both a short drive from town. Charge at the Roseburg Supercharger before parking for the night.

Camp →

Day 5 · Wednesday

Portland, full day

Gardens, a mansion view, and a walk in the woods, all inside city limits — back-to-back with no dead time between.

Morning$21.95 admission

Washington Park — Portland Japanese Garden

Widely considered one of the most authentic Japanese gardens outside of Japan — five distinct garden styles across 12 acres. The International Rose Test Garden is a short walk away in the same park and is free.

Pittock Mansion

The best skyline view in Portland — on a clear day you can see Mount Hood, Mount St. Helens, and Mount Adams from the front lawn. The grounds are free even if you skip the house tour.

Day 6 · Thursday

Multnomah Falls → south toward Ashland

Gorge waterfalls at sunrise, then get a real head start on the drive home — this is what turns Day 7 from a 500-mile slog into an easy last leg.

Early morningFree

Multnomah Falls

Oregon's tallest waterfall, and worth the early wake-up — the parking lot fills fast and it's crowded by mid-morning. The paved path up to Benson Bridge is short and easy, with the best straight-on view of the falls.

Map it →
🚘
~10 min · same stretch of the Gorge
Morning0.4 mi round trip

Latourell Falls

A second, much less crowded waterfall a few minutes down the Historic Columbia River Highway — a quick, easy add before you turn around and head south.

Retrace I-5 south. This is a driving-focused stretch by design — the sightseeing already happened this morning, and the goal now is covering ground while there's still daylight.

Before You Go

Good to Know

The logistics that actually matter for a solo, non-long-range Tesla trip like this one.

↗

Why this route doesn't backtrack

Crater Lake has entrances on both the south (OR-62, from Ashland/Medford) and north (Hwy 138, toward Roseburg) sides. Driving in one way and out the other turns what's normally a there-and-back day trip into forward progress — no wasted miles, and two waterfall stops (Toketee Falls, Latourell Falls) added along the way.

⚡

Charging strategy

  • Redding ↔ Mount Shasta: ~62 mi — comfortable
  • Mount Shasta ↔ Medford: crosses the Siskiyou Summit grade — charge full before this one
  • No Supercharging inside Crater Lake NP — top off in Medford first
  • Medford → Roseburg → Eugene/Springfield → Portland: all standard I-5 corridor Superchargers, no long gaps
🕹

Camp Mode & charging order

Charge before you set up for the night, not after — Camp Mode keeps climate and power running all night and will eat a real chunk of your charge by morning. Arriving at camp already full avoids waking up short.

🌅

Crater Lake in October

Rim Drive is typically open early July through late October depending on weather, but Mazama Campground and the in-park cabins close for the season by late September — that's why this stays a drive-through, not an overnight.

🌡

Weather window

Early October is the sweet spot for this route — past the summer crowds and heat, before the Pacific Northwest's rainy season really sets in (usually mid-to-late October onward). Check the Crater Lake forecast the morning of Day 3, since an early mountain storm can close Rim Drive sections with little notice.

Cali's Oregon Road Trip

San Francisco → Mount Shasta → Ashland → Crater Lake → Roseburg → Eugene → Portland → Ashland → home

Six nights, one Tesla, before the rain comes.
